clue.text: Briefly Commander Bond's put in danger

parts.note: Com. is a recognised short form of the rank of commander
a bond is a pledge or undertaking, a promise

explanation.surface: A naval officer and a spy named Bond, briefly mentioned as being exposed to peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' tempts toward the spy, but here it is a pledge; the 's is just 'is' linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise something, such as security or a position, is to expose it to risk.

clue.text: Rabbit caught beaver, perhaps

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a beaver was a type of felt hat, so it is an example of headwear

explanation.surface: A rabbit has been caught by a beaver, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang for talk (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to rabbit on is to talk at length, which is a synonym for natter or gossip.

clue.text: Mother ordered Garnier product made with vegetable oil

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters of Garnier are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Mum bought a Garnier cosmetic product containing vegetable oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Garnier is a cosmetics brand, which steers the surface away from food.
explanation.definitionFit: This butter substitute is a spread manufactured from vegetable oils.

clue.text: Managed cattle here, initially?

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letters of the words cattle and here

explanation.surface: Someone ran a cattle operation in this spot to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a place where cattle are managed.
explanation.definitionFit: A large farm where livestock are reared is exactly a place where cattle are managed.

clue.text: Trades book and gets cover removed

parts.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament

indicators.note: a cover sits on top, so in a down clue the top letter of gets is taken off

explanation.surface: Someone books something and gets its cover taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover removed' drops only the first letter of GETS, leaving ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Markets, as a verb, means sells or promotes goods, i.e. trades them.

clue.text: Dubious guess

definitions.meaning: questionable or not to be trusted
to suppose or surmise something without proof

explanation.surface: A doubtful guess.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means questionable; as a verb it means to suppose or surmise.

clue.text: Further returns in private bank

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Money goes back again into a private bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to help it along, a synonym of assist or support.

clue.text: Black range is essential for a witch

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
range means scope or space, which is room

explanation.surface: A black cooking range is a must-have for any witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests a kitchen stove beside the witch's cauldron, but it means room as in scope.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches traditionally ride a broomstick, so it is a key piece of their kit.

clue.text: Intimidated small number clutching at study being overturned

indicators.note: clutching shows the first word holds the next one inside it

parts.note: three is a small number

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: A few people were frightened when their study was turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatened and intimidated are synonyms: both mean menaced or bullied.

clue.text: In favour of wearing an aid in the kitchen?

indicators.note: wearing shows one piece is enclosed by the other, as clothes enclose a body

parts.note: pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Supporting the idea of wearing a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' fits the definition neatly, since this kitchen aid is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook ties on this garment to protect their clothes, so it is a help when cooking.

clue.text: River rose high — it holds a lot of water

definitions.text: it holds a lot of water

indicators.note: high, as in intoxicated, signals that the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The river level rose sharply, as it holds plenty of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' reads as the flood level but is the anagram signal for RIVER ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made lake or tank used to store a water supply holds a large volume.

clue.text: Most fruitful case to follow scripture lessons

indicators.note: to follow says the case comes after the lessons

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, school scripture lessons
a chest is a box or case

explanation.surface: The most rewarding case study comes after scripture class.
explanation.walkthrough: RI stands for religious instruction, the old name for scripture lessons in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich soil or a rich source is abundant and productive, so the superlative means most productive.

clue.text: A permit held by the runner?

indicators.note: held by shows the permit sits inside the word the

parts.note: let means allow or permit

explanation.surface: A licence is in the possession of the runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is one example of a sportsperson, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mark gets married in dazed state

indicators.note: in shows the abbreviation goes inside the dazed state

parts.note: a coma is a deep state of unconsciousness

explanation.surface: Mark gets married while in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a groom's name but means a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark separates parts of a sentence.

clue.text: Unfortunately cities fail to provide resources

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, cities fail to provide resources.
explanation.definitionFit: Facilities are amenities or services provided for use, so they are resources.

clue.text: Article I criticise about 'brutes'

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about indicates the word for criticise is turned round

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: Someone admits to criticising an article about brutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutes, in the older sense, are beasts, non-human creatures.

clue.text: Lay a rug — with regret, that has to be taken up

parts.note: a mat is a small rug

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone lays a rug and regrets it, so it must be lifted again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb about the rug, but it is the adjective meaning non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are non-specialists, so lay means non-professional, unpaid.

clue.text: A tragedy's beginning in that place?

definitions.text: A tragedy's beginning in that place?

indicators.note: in shows those letters go inside the word for that place

parts.note: there means in or at that place

indicators.note: beginning asks for the opening letter of the word tragedy

explanation.surface: A tragedy opens in that venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the venue: where a tragedy gets its start, on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays, including tragedies, are first performed in a playhouse.

clue.text: Fighter is swimming predator in African rivers

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving freely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fighter is swimming among predators in African rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: This fierce, sharp-toothed fish hunts in African rivers such as the Zambezi.

clue.text: Country dancing nice with lad

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Country dancing is nice with a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country dancing' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition and 'dancing' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a North Atlantic island nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Illness in facility headed by detectives

indicators.note: headed by puts the detectives at the top of the down answer

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: A sickness in a building run by police detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' looks like a building but means ease of doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disease and illness are synonyms for sickness or ailment.

clue.text: Wash out most of military clothing

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: fatigues are soldiers' work uniforms

explanation.surface: Washing out most of a soldier's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash out' looks like laundry, but it means exhaust or tire out.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash someone out is to exhaust them, the same as to tire them.

clue.text: Fixed chapter from rising American editor

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means those letters are read upwards

parts.note: of can mean from, as in a man of Kent

explanation.surface: A chapter was fixed by an editor from America on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed gaze or attention is one that is concentrated and intent.

clue.text: Is to take legal action against children

parts.note: to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: Someone is going to take their children to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for a person's offspring.

clue.text: Toff and wife stuck in traffic

indicators.note: stuck in shows the letter is lodged inside the other word

parts.note: to traffic is to deal or sell

explanation.surface: A posh man and his wife are stuck in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like road congestion, but it is the verb meaning trade. A toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is old slang for a fashionable, well-dressed gentleman, a synonym of toff.

clue.text: Help from gullible person, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like what is spoken

parts.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Getting help from a gullible person, by all accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is aid or assistance given in a time of need.

clue.text: Rotten pears not oddly tender

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten

indicators.note: not oddly says to skip the odd letters of pears and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: Rotten pears are not, oddly, soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' suggests soft fruit, but it is the verb meaning to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender a bid or resignation is to present or propose it formally.

clue.text: Raised a large sum of money for Scotch

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal

explanation.surface: Plenty of money was raised to buy whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but it is the verb meaning to put an end to a rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan or rumour is to put an end to it, i.e. halt it.

clue.text: Same rice prepared around 100 desserts

indicators.note: around shows the rearranged letters surround the numeral
prepared suggests the letters are made into something new

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: The same rice dish is prepared for a hundred puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges SAME RICE into ICE REAMS, which goes 'around' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen sweets made from cream are common examples of puddings.

clue.text: Female informally is not dim

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: A woman, speaking casually, says she is not stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dim' suggests stupid, but it means barely visible.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint light or outline is weak or hard to see, a synonym of dim.

clue.text: Odour getting rid of male hawk

indicators.note: getting rid of means that letter is taken out

parts.note: a smell is an odour

explanation.surface: A smell that drives off a male bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to peddle goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to peddle them in the street, i.e. offer them for money.

clue.text: What the captain possibly shows the Queen in metal vessel

indicators.note: in shows the royal initials go inside the other pieces

parts.note: lead is a metal
a ship is a vessel
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A captain shows the Queen around a metal-hulled vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain, of a team or ship, is expected to display command and guidance.
